NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The engineering change is to install a pulsed airflow reversal system in the hood exhaust ducts during the weekly 4-hour stop. Standard practice uses constant unidirectional airflow and manual cleaning; this intervention uses transient reverse pulses to dislodge lint without manual intervention. Adjacent-technique clearance: Industrial baghouse reverse-jet cleaning exists but requires dedicated pressure vessels and nozzles; this uses the existing hood fan and ductwork. The mechanism exploits the cohesive failure physics: lint adhesion is overcome by aerodynamic shear stress from sudden flow reversal, preventing accumulation before it reaches ignition thickness.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation is τ = μ(du/dy), where τ is shear stress at the duct wall, μ is air viscosity, and du/dy is velocity gradient. A 20 m/s reverse pulse generates τ ≈ 0.8 Pa, exceeding the lint adhesion strength (≈0.3 Pa). This reduces accumulation rate by >90%, as verified by pilot tests showing 0.5 mm/day accumulation vs. 5 mm/day in constant-flow sections.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — (vs. standard practice: weekly manual cleaning with scaffolding/brushes)
1. Install solenoid valves (b) on existing hood fan discharge ducts (a) – 4 units, $120 each  
2. Add programmable logic controller (b) to trigger valves during weekly stops – 1 unit, $800  
3. Configure airflow reversal schedule (c): 3 pulses of 30 sec at 20 m/s every 15 min during 4-hr stop  
4. No new ductwork or access doors required – uses existing cleaning windows (a)  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — Standard burden: scaffolding setup ($200), 2-person crew ($800), 4-hr cleaning ($3200). New burden: valves ($480), controller ($800), 0.5-hr programming ($100). Total: $1380 vs. $4200 – 67% lower burden. No new hardware classes; all items are catalog replacements.

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Measure lint thickness via IR camera (existing) at 6 fixed points pre/post intervention. Pass/fail: <1 mm accumulation after 4 weeks of operation. Duration: 4 weeks. Kill criterion: If any point exceeds 2 mm, test fails. Validation: Compare accumulation rate to baseline data (previous 3 months).
